articles.title: Breaking: Vande Mataram Row Escalates as Amit Shah Attacks Congress Over Two-Verse Decision
articles.description: The political battle over Vande Mataram has intensified after the Congress Working Committee decided that only the first two verses of the national song will be sung at party programmes. Congress has described the song as an emotional issue, while the BJP has accused the opposition party of pursuing appeasement politics. Union Home Minister Amit Shah strongly criticised the Congress decision, alleging that the party was following its 1937 resolution and repeating what he described as a historical mistake. Shah claimed that the decision taken in 1937 to restrict the song was linked to efforts to accommodate Muslim opinion and alleged that it contributed to the circumstances surrounding Partition. He further said that the Narendra Modi government had corrected that position and given the national song a legal framework. The BJP has announced plans to raise the issue before the public and in legislative forums. BJP president Nitin Nabin also accused the Congress of disrespecting Vande Mataram and alleged that the party had now converted the controversy into an official policy. The dispute gained further momentum after a video from the Congress headquarters on Independence Day appeared to show Sonia Gandhi signalling during the singing of the song. Congress leaders disputed the BJP's interpretation of the incident. The party has maintained that its position follows the 1937 Congress Working Committee decision, citing concerns over the religious references in later verses. Congress leaders have hit back at the BJP, invoking historical figures including Mahatma Gandhi, Rabindranath Tagore, Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Subhas Chandra Bose. With both sides taking sharply opposing positions, the Vande Mataram controversy has emerged as a major political flashpoint, bringing history, nationalism, secularism and electoral politics into the centre of the debate.

ALERT! On Mojtaba's Order, Houthis Ready Huge Buildup To Seize Another Key Maritime Point?
articles.description: Yemen’s internationally recognised government is warning that the Iran-backed Houthis may be seeking to strengthen their position around the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Yemen’s Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told AFP that the group is working to create conditions to potentially seize control of the waterway, while expanding its presence along Yemen’s western coastline and seeking influence over strategic Red Sea islands. The Bab al-Mandeb connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and is a crucial route for global shipping. The Houthis currently do not control the strait itself, although they hold the major Red Sea port of Hodeidah farther north. The reported buildup comes amid continuing tensions and previous Houthi attacks involving ships and maritime infrastructure in the region.

articles.description: A UAE-linked oil tanker seized by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz is reportedly moving toward the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas, according to Iran’s semi-official Fars news agency. The vessel was initially scheduled to sail toward the UAE’s Jebel Ali port before being stopped in the northern corridor near Qeshm Island. The reported seizure comes as Tehran imposes tighter requirements on vessels crossing the strategic waterway, including designated routes and permission from Iranian authorities. Iran has also restricted passage for vessels linked to Israel or the United States. The developments highlight growing tensions over control of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global energy route connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.
